# The Oregon Trail

A wagon, five names, and the road from Independence to the Willamette. The year is 1848. A score is written only if someone arrives.

## Start

Return leaves the title and opens the menu. On the road, Return stops the wagon. R from the title, or from a finished trail, starts the next party and skips the title. Q on the daily menu asks if you want to abandon the trail.

## Who you are

You name all five. The first name is the wagon leader.

- A banker from Boston starts with $1600. The score stands as scored.
- A carpenter from Ohio starts with $800. The score is doubled.
- A farmer from Illinois starts with $400. The score is tripled.

You can leave in March, April, May, June, or July.

## Matt's

A yoke is two oxen and costs $40. Matt recommends three. Food is twenty cents a pound. The wagon holds 2000 pounds. Clothing is $10 a set. Ammunition is $2 a box of 20 bullets. A spare wheel, axle, or tongue is $10.

Forts sell the same goods, and the price rises as you go west.

## On the road

1. Continue. The wagon rolls a day at a time.
2. Check supplies.
3. Look at the map.
4. Change pace. Steady, strenuous, or grueling.
5. Change rations. Filling, meager, or bare bones.
6. Rest, up to twenty days.
7. Trade.
8. Hunt. Arrows or WASD move. Space shoots. Each shot is one bullet. Q goes back to the wagon. You can carry 100 pounds back.
9. Matt's, while you are still in Independence. Buy supplies, at a fort. Talk to people, everywhere else.

## Water and the end

Rivers ask you to ford, caulk and float, wait, or ask how deep it is. The Columbia is a raft. Arrows steer. The channel opens on the right.

If the wagon leader dies, the screen says so in the old way. The rest of the party can press on. When the whole party is dead, the run ends with no score. The Oregon Top Ten stays in this browser.
